updates.name: James B. Heffernan
updates.bio: Associate professor of ecosystem ecology and ecohydrology in Duke University's Nicholas School of the Environment. His research examines major shifts in the structure of streams, rivers and wetlands, centred on feedbacks among biological, physical and biogeochemical processes, and increasingly carries local-ecosystem approaches to regional and continental scales.
updates.research_interests: major changes in ecosystem structure of streams, rivers and wetlands; ecohydrology; feedbacks among ecological, physical and biogeochemical processes; regional- to continental-scale ecology

updates.name: James B. Shanley
updates.bio: Research hydrologist with the USGS New England Water Science Center, now listed by USGS as a former employee, whose work centred on Vermont's Sleepers River Research Watershed in Danville: headwater stream chemistry, dissolved organic matter and mercury transport, snow and soil-frost monitoring, and the value of long-term watershed records.

updates.name: Jan A. Newton
updates.bio: Biological oceanographer at the University of Washington: senior principal oceanographer at the Applied Physics Laboratory and affiliate professor in the School of Oceanography. She has been executive director of NANOOS since 2005, when its founding agreement took effect, and studies coastal and estuarine dynamics and how climate and human activity affect water quality.

updates.name: Jayne Belnap
updates.bio: USGS research ecologist at the Southwest Biological Science Center in Moab, Utah. For about three decades she has studied dryland and rangeland ecosystems, especially biological soil crusts, how climate change will affect drylands, and low-cost restoration to curb soil erosion; she was elected a Fellow of the Ecological Society of America in 2015.
updates.research_interests: biological soil crusts; dryland and rangeland ecosystems; sustainable land management; climate change effects on drylands; restoration to reduce soil erosion; desert and grassland ecosystems
updates.current_affiliation: U.S. Geological Survey, Southwest Biological Science Center
